queue.tree_name: The American Oak of the Pekingtuin
queue.recognise: The very large oak standing alone on the lawn, with a trunk over five metres round. Not the smaller tree inside the steel ring with the poem on it, which stands about sixty metres west.
queue.story:
Planted around 1850 and now 5.52 metres around, the American oak of the Pekingtuin is the heaviest trunk in Baarn's village centre, and it stands five minutes from the railway station in a park that costs nothing to enter.

Quercus rubra comes from the eastern United States, and the Dutch call it the Amerikaanse eik. This one went into the ground as an exotic in the private grounds of Villa Peking, decades before the railway and the villa quarter around it took their present shape. What is left of that garden is the park: a wide lawn carrying very large trees, most of them oaks, with a bandstand from 1948 at one end. queue.recognise: The single large plane on the open lawn directly in front of the town hall at Stationsweg 18, with the patchwork bark planes carry and a trunk over four and a half metres round.
queue.story:
Over four and a half metres round and roughly 130 years old, the plane on the lawn at Stationsweg 18 is a century older than the town hall it stands in front of.

That building went up in 1993, on the footprint of a villa from 1897, and the national tree register suggests the plane may have been planted while the villa was being built. The same register records its condition as good despite that building history, which is worth something for a tree that has had construction work inside its root plate. It belongs to the municipality and stands in full view of the through road, which is why the register calls the position a fine one.
